Judge censured after jailing woman for profanity (2014)

Judge Dennis Wiley was publicly censured by the Michigan Judicial Tenure Commission on March 26, 2014, after he put a woman in jail for 10 days for cursing at the courthouse.

LaRue Ford came to the Niles courthouse on December 4, 2012, to pay traffic fines and remove a hold on her driver's license. Court clerks said that she used profanities when told that she needed to pay a $45 reinstatement fee to remove the suspension. Judge Wiley overheard the clerks talking about the interaction with Ford and ordered that she be sent to his courtroom when she came back. Upon her return, Wiley charged Ford with contempt of court and set a bail of $5,000 or a 10 percent cash deposit. After spending a night in jail, the $500 bail was posted and she left. During the hearing on December 18, Wiley increased the bail to $5,000 in cash, and Ford spent another 10 nights in jail.[10]

The bond was lowered and Ford was released on December 28, after the American Civil Liberties Union filed an appeal of bond, which was approved by Judge Alfred Butzbaugh. The county prosecutor declined to prosecute her contempt of court charge, and the charge was dropped by Judge Charles LaSata on January 11.[10]

The Judicial Tenure Commission found that Wiley violated the following canons of the Michigan Code of Judicial Conduct:

3A(1): "he did not faithfully execute the law and maintain his professional competence when he commenced indirect contempt proceedings based only on unsworn conversations with his staff"[11] 3A(4): "he received communications regarding Ms. Ford’s conduct from court staff, after the commencement of proceedings, and directed staff to provide the information to the prosecuting attorney and directed staff to prepare affidavits concerning the events of December 4, 2012 and did not advise Ms. Ford’s counsel of these communications"[11]

For my current employer? I would never concoct any sinister plans. I'm a relatively good person working for good people.

Of course, I've had my fair share of horrible employers. Here are a couple of the more memorable quits:

(1) Worked for a library, and it was a fantastic job up until there was a shake-up in management. My boss's boss (and his boss) were some of the worst people I have ever worked for. It got to a point where I had just had enough of it. I went in early before my shift, asked my boss if I could speak with her, and then effectively resigned. My boss loved loves me because I was one of her best employees, and she told me she was sorry to see me go, but that she completely understood my feelings on the matter, wished me the best, and told me she would always be willing to act as a professional reference for me. Minutes after I resigned, I called one of my co-worker friends, and I told her, "hey, I just quit." And since she had felt the same way I did, she said, "really? I'm going to quit, too, then." So she went in later that afternoon, and resigned. She reported to me that my boss had a complete emotional breakdown, because she lost two of her best employees within just a few hours -- and we were like 2/3s of the people that had been cross-trained in different departments. Even though I quit because I hated the work environment, I still have tons of connections there, with several people willing to act as references for me.

(2) I once worked at a place that rented formal attire, which I did through prom and wedding season (spring/summer). It was my job to clean rental shoes for 12 hours a day. The job was awful as it was, but one day, management came to us and increased our quotas to the point of it being an impossible job. I took my break early, went to punch out, and on the top of my time-card, I wrote in huge letters, "I QUIT!" I still haven't returned from my break.
